title: dazpy viewport snapshot API (_viewport.py)
description:
Add a viewport capture method to the dazpy SDK so Python scripts can save the active DAZ Studio 3D viewport to a PNG/JPEG file without triggering a full iRay render.

## Why
The ComfyUI pipeline needs a fast source image. iRay renders take minutes; the OpenGL viewport preview takes under a second. dazpy currently has no way to capture the viewport — only full renders via _render.py. This is also generally useful for thumbnailing, scene inspection, and live preview workflows.

## What needs to be done
- Create dazpy/_viewport.py with a DazViewport class
- capture(path, width=None, height=None) method using DzViewport::captureToFile() via DazScript:
  MainWindow.getViewportMgr().getActiveViewport().get3DViewport().captureToFile(path)
- Optional: set_size(w, h) / get_size() using DzViewport geometry
- Add DazViewport to dazpy/__init__.py exports
- Add unit tests (mock-based) in tests_dazpy.py
- Add integration tests (gated @skip_no_daz) in tests_dazpy_integration.py

## Design decisions
- Use captureToFile() not grabFramebuffer() — captureToFile writes to disk directly, simpler path
- Return the output path as a string for confirmation
- Accept optional width/height to temporarily resize the viewport before capture (restore after)

## Acceptance criteria
- dazpy.DazViewport().capture('C:/tmp/snap.png') writes a valid PNG to disk
- Unit tests pass without a live server
- Integration test passes against a running DAZ Studio instance

title: Add POST /render endpoint (single render, async)
description:
VN production workflows need to trigger DAZ renders programmatically. Without a render endpoint, every render requires manual GUI interaction, making batch sprite production impossible to automate.

Implement POST /render that accepts a render job, enqueues it through the existing AsyncRequestManager, executes on the main thread, and returns a request_id immediately.

Request body schema:
- output_path (required, absolute path)
- width / height (optional, override scene render settings)
- format: png|jpg|tiff|exr (optional, inferred from output_path extension)
- camera (optional, null = active camera)
- engine (optional, null = scene default: iray|3delight|filament)
- figure / morphs (optional, single-figure morph dict)
- figures (optional, list of {name, morphs} for multi-figure scenes)
- iray_samples (optional quality override)

Render jobs use id prefix 'rnd-' and flow through the existing processNextAsyncRequest() path as a special request type. The server generates a DazScript snippet from the morph dict, applies morphs via findPropertyByLabel(), then calls App.getRenderMgr().render(opts). Unknown morph names are silently skipped (non-fatal). Status/result polling via existing /requests/:id/status and /requests/:id/result endpoints.

Open questions to resolve during implementation:
1. morph reset between variants (reset_morphs flag needed?)
2. Figure lookup fallback: error vs fall back to primary figure
3. Add isRender flag to AsyncRequest struct in AsyncRequestManager.h
design:
1. reset_morphs flag: Add reset_morphs: bool to POST /render request body. When true, reset all figure morphs to zero on the main thread before applying the morphs dict and rendering. Required for correct variant rendering when the same figure is reused across batch jobs.

2. Figure lookup failure = error: On figure lookup failure, return an HTTP error (not a silent fallback). Before any render step begins, run a validation pass over the entire figures array to identify all figure references and validate they resolve to scene nodes. This surfaces all bad references at once rather than failing mid-render.

3. RequestType enum instead of isRender bool: Add RequestType enum (REQUEST_TYPE_SCRIPT, REQUEST_TYPE_RENDER) to AsyncRequest struct rather than a boolean isRender flag. title: Main orchestrator script (main.py)
description:
Build the main.py entry point that wires together the viewport snapshot, file watcher, and ComfyUI submission into a single runnable workflow.

- Always print the output path at the end so it can be piped or opened programmatically

title: File watcher module (file_watcher.py)
description:
Build a file watcher that monitors a directory for a new image file and triggers a callback when the file is fully written.

## Why
DAZ Studio's captureToFile() is fire-and-forget from the script side — it writes to disk but the dazpy client doesn't know the exact moment the file is ready. A file watcher decouples the capture trigger from the ComfyUI submission and handles the write-completion race condition reliably.

## What needs to be done
- FileWatcher class using the watchdog library:
  - watch(directory: str, callback: Callable[[str], None], pattern: str = '*.png', timeout: float = 30.0) -> str
  - Blocks until a matching file appears in the directory and is fully written
  - Write-completion detection: poll file size until it stops growing (100ms interval, 3 stable readings)
  - Returns the full path of the detected file
  - Raises TimeoutError if timeout elapses with no file
- Also support async-style: watch_async() that starts a background thread and calls callback when ready
- cleanup: remove the handler after first match (one-shot mode by default)

## Design decisions
- watchdog Observer is heavier than polling but handles network drives and non-inotify systems correctly on Windows
- One-shot mode is correct for this pipeline (one capture → one submission)
- Write-completion by size stability is more reliable than a fixed sleep

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit test: mock watchdog events, assert callback fires with correct path
- Integration test: write a file to a temp dir, assert watch() returns the path

title: ComfyUI HTTP API client module
description:
Build a self-contained ComfyUI client module (comfyui_client.py) that handles all HTTP communication with a local ComfyUI instance.

## Why
ComfyUI exposes a REST+WebSocket API that is not officially documented but is well understood from community usage. Encapsulating it in a client class keeps the orchestrator clean and makes the client independently testable.

## What needs to be done
- ComfyUIClient class with:
  - __init__(base_url='http://127.0.0.1:8188', client_id=None)
  - upload_image(path: str) -> str — POST /upload/image, returns 'subfolder/filename'
  - queue_prompt(workflow: dict) -> str — POST /prompt, returns prompt_id
  - get_history(prompt_id: str) -> dict — GET /history/{prompt_id}
  - wait_for_result(prompt_id: str, timeout: float = 120.0) -> dict — polls get_history until outputs appear
  - download_image(filename: str, subfolder: str = '', folder_type: str = 'output') -> bytes — GET /view

- client_id is a UUID generated once per instance, used in prompt submissions
- No WebSocket — polling is sufficient for batch workflows

title: Add POST /render/batch endpoint for variant rendering
description:
VN production requires rendering many variants of the same scene (expressions, poses) — often 10-30 per character setup. Submitting each individually requires many round trips and makes orchestration harder.

Implement POST /render/batch that accepts a base config plus a list of variants, enqueues each variant as an independent async render request, and returns all request_ids in one response.

Request schema:
  base: {camera, width, height, engine, figure} — shared settings
  variants: [{output_path, morphs, figures, ...overrides}] — per-render settings

Each variant is an independent AsyncRequest with isRender=true. Returns:
  {batch_id: 'bat-...', request_ids: [...], total: N}

Key design point: variants render sequentially (DAZ cannot render two scenes simultaneously), but the HTTP client can interleave other requests between polls. Document both usage patterns:
  Pattern A: submit full batch upfront, poll all request_ids
  Pattern B: submit one at a time, use setup between renders for complex scene changes

Atomicity: if variant N fails, variants N+1..M still render. Per-variant errors in results.
notes: Implemented. POST /render/batch accepts {base, variants:[]}. Base provides optional defaults (camera, width, height, engine, figure/figures, reset_morphs). Each variant requires output_path; merges with base for remaining fields. Figure merge: variant figures/figure wins; variant morphs+single base figure merges morphs (variant overrides). All variants validated and pre-flighted before any are enqueued (fail-fast). Enqueue failures mid-batch return 503 with partial count. Response: {batch_id:'bat-...', request_ids:[...], total:N}. Each rnd-id compatible with existing /requests/:id/status, /requests/:id/result, and GET /render/:id/progress endpoints. Max 100 variants per batch.
